content.title: About
content.content: Prunes are dried plums of special varieties (Prunus domestica) that are high in sugar and can be dried with the pit without fermenting. Prunes have dark, sticky, soft flesh with a sweet-tart flavor. They are eaten as a snack and added to desserts, baked goods, porridge, sauces, and meat dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Special plum varieties with a high sugar content are used for prunes.
In the United States, prunes have been allowed to be called dried plums since 2000.
One of the best-known production regions is Agen in France.
Prunes have long been paired with meat, such as chicken, duck, and beef, in Russian and European cooking.
Plums used for prunes are usually smaller and more oval than table varieties.

items.title: Contain fiber and sorbitol
items.content: These compounds help keep bowel movements regular.

items.title: Contain potassium
items.content: Potassium supports normal blood pressure and muscle function.

items.title: Contain vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K plays a role in blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Contain polyphenols
items.content: The phenolic compounds in prunes have antioxidant properties.

items.title: Studied for bone health
items.content: Prunes are being studied in relation to maintaining bone density, but evidence is still limited.

items.title: Diarrhea and bloating
items.content: Because of fiber and sorbitol, a large amount of prunes can cause diarrhea, gas, and cramps.

items.title: Sugar and calories
items.content: Prunes are high in calories and sugar, so portions should be moderate.

items.title: Potassium
items.content: People with kidney disease who need to limit potassium should consult a doctor.

items.title: Sulfites and pits
items.content: Some prunes are treated with sulfites, and fruit sold with pits may contain a pit that can damage teeth.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Prunes can be eaten as a snack or added to porridge, yogurt, baked goods, desserts, sauces, and meat or poultry dishes. To soften hard prunes, soak them in warm water for a while. A small handful is enough.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store prunes in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place; they keep longer in the refrigerator. Discard fruit that is moldy, smells sour, or shows signs of fermentation.
